messages:
elaine (prod): FYI I pushed a short RFC draft for serving economics focused on small/short queries. looking for quick take on acceptance criteria and what we can actually ship in next quarter. link: https://rwd/internal/rfc/serving-econ-small-queries

sam (eng-ml): reading it now. main tradeoff i saw: batching helps cost but for 1-4 token responses it usually adds wait due to batching timers. we should consider an "always-low-latency" lane vs "cost-optimized" lane.

ravi (eng-platform): agree. can we define SLOs per lane? e.g. LL lane = p95 < 120ms for median 8-token responses, cost lane = target 40% lower token-cost for same throughput.

elaine (prod): @sam @ravi yep. also customer asks: prefer deterministic quant profiles for embeddings/short completions. they care about quality regressions.

jess (sre): quick flag — autoscale warmup matters. if LL lane scales from 0, cold GPUs + container startup kills p95. need reserved min capacity for LL or instant scale hooks.

maya (cust-suc): echo customer feedback: enterprise A saw hallucinations after int8 quant on instruction prompts. they want an eval harness before auto-recommendation.

sam (eng-ml): proposal: in RFC acceptance criteria include: 1) quality delta vs baseline < 1.0 BLEU-like (or automated eval metric we use) for target prompt set; 2) LL lane p95 latency targets; 3) cost reduction targets for cost lane.

elaine (prod): can we make those specific? we need measurable gates for launch.

sam (eng-ml): specifics: - quality: avg ROUGE-L drop < 0.8% on our short-instruction set (1000 prompts) for quantized models - LL lane p95 < 120ms for 8-token responses and p99 < 220ms under steady load of 150rps - cost lane unit-token cost <= 0.6x baseline for batch-friendly workloads

ravi (eng-platform): technical constraints: batching window ideally < 8ms for LL lane, and dynamic batching for cost lane up to 40ms. Also prefix/KV caching should be opt-in and TTL per-customer.

jess (sre): rollout plan: canary 5% traffic -> monitor p95/p99, quality regressions (eval set), and error rate. automatic rollback if quality alerts > 3x baseline or p99 > threshold for 5m.

maya (cust-suc): add acceptance step: run customer-provided prompt set in staging and let them sign-off for quant recommendations. this is required for enterprise private deployments.

sam (eng-ml): added a short config example to RFC for ops defaults, feel free to copy: ```
serve.lanes:
  - name: low-latency
    batching: {window_ms: 8, max_batch: 8}
    min_reserved_replicas: 2
    quant_profile: fp16
  - name: cost-optimized
    batching: {window_ms: 40, max_batch: 64}
    quant_profile: int8
cache:
  prefix_kv: {enabled: true, ttl_s: 300, per_customer: true}
```

elaine (prod): nice. two questions: 1) do we need a UX surface to pick lane per-route? 2) should traffic routing be automatic (policy) or manual opt-in per customer?

ravi (eng-platform): platform prefers policy with override. default routing rules: latency-sensitive routes go to LL lane (based on route hint or token-threshold), else cost lane. allow per-customer pin.

jess (sre): ops checklist: metric dashboards (p95/p99, cost/token, eval-quality), alerting (quality regressions, error spikes), runbook for rollback. i'll stub runbook after RFC approval.

elaine (prod): thanks. action items: @sam update RFC with the numeric acceptance criteria, add canary thresholds, include customer sign-off step; @ravi add routing policy example; @jess add runbook stub. target to merge RFC by EOD Friday so eng can scope next sprint.

deploy-bot: PR created by sam: https://rwd/internal/pulls/4321 (serving-econ-small-queries-rfc)

sam (eng-ml): on it, will update by noon tomorrow.

maya (cust-suc): i'll coordinate with the customer to get a short prompt set and sign-off timeline.

elaine (prod): great — thanks everyone :rocket:
